{"id":"persona-qbnm.7","title":"oidc: verify the cached token against the issuer's JWKS","description":"Split from persona-qbnm.6, whose tailscale half landed in 1365300. oidc is not a trust-assertion problem at all: a cached ID token carries a real signature that could be checked against the issuer's JWKS and simply is not. That makes it a verifier to write, not a trust to assert -- the opposite of tailscale, which is why bundling them was wrong.

MEASURED STATE (2026-09-15): oidc.rs:119-168 reads ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json and ~/.azure/{msal_token_cache.json,accessTokens.json}, decodes the payload with NO signature check (:37-44), and uses exp for freshness only (:57-61). Nothing in the workspace fetches a JWKS or verifies a third-party JWT: jsonwebtoken appears only in hire-core/src/signer.rs, hire-core/src/trust_bundle.rs:60-70 (which already parses a JwkSet and finds a key by kid -- reusable shape) and hire-grpc/src/service.rs. There is no HTTPS client anywhere; hyper-util is the UDS transport, not a TLS client. A discovery + JWKS fetch needs a new dependency.

THE BLOCKER IS auth_time, NOT THE FETCH. VerifiedToken's doc comment (claim.rs) requires authenticated_at to come from the token's auth_time and requires the constructor to REFUSE when auth_time is absent, because stamping SystemTime::now() would make every cached token permanently session-fresh -- persona-ogiv's bug restored on the OIDC path, beside a type that looks like it prevents exactly that. auth_time is OPTIONAL in OIDC Core unless max_age or auth_time was requested at authorization time, and neither gcloud ADC nor Azure v2.0 generally includes it. So the honest outcome of doing all the JWKS work is that the verifying constructor refuses most real cached tokens and oidc still contributes nothing.

DECIDE THAT FIRST, before writing any fetch code. Refusing is correct per the type's own contract; the alternative is changing what authenticated_at means, which reopens the bug the field exists to prevent. If the answer is 'refuse', this bead is cheap and mostly documentation -- and that is a constraint deleting a category of work, not a failure.

SECOND OPEN QUESTION: Evidence::binds_to returns true unconditionally for IdpVerified (claim.rs), with a ponytail naming the token nonce as the intended binding. A cached token carries a nonce from someone else's login flow, not hire's challenge, so the replay window stays open unless that is decided too.","acceptance_criteria":"A decision recorded on what to do when auth_time is absent, before any JWKS fetching code exists.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-16T01:37:15.883403454Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-16T01:37:15.883403454Z","labels":["attestor","driver"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-qbnm.7","depends_on_id":"persona-qbnm","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-16T01:37:15.907496363Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DECIDED 2026-09-16 BY MARK, and the type change landed in 7e1bcde ahead of any network code: a verified token with no auth_time yields Iaa2 with NO presence, dated at the instant hire checked the signature; auth_time present yields Iaa2 with Session presence dated at auth_time. THE BLOCKER THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERION NAMED IS THEREFORE SETTLED -- what remains is ordinary work.

THE REASONING, so nobody re-opens it: the signature and auth_time are two different claims. The signature proves an identity provider issued this token for this subject (ASSURANCE); auth_time proves a human authenticated at a moment (PRESENCE). persona-3tly holds those are independent axes. Refusing the whole token because one half was missing threw away the half that was present, and made the source dead on the common case -- auth_time is REQUIRED in OIDC Core only when the client asked for max_age or requested it as an essential claim, and hire does not mint these tokens, so gcloud and the Azure CLI decided it years ago for unrelated reasons. The undated arm is the shape DaemonAssertion already has for the same reason, and dating it at the check is honest because it dates the check rather than the human. persona-ogiv's bug stays closed: no path claims presence without auth_time. Both arms are mutation-tested.

REJECTED: falling back to iat. auth_time <= iat always, so iat claims the human authenticated MORE recently than they did, and a token minted from a refresh token an hour ago can stand for an authentication from a month ago. Fail-open and undetectable from the token itself.

WHAT IS LEFT, all ordinary: a TLS client (no HTTPS dependency exists in the workspace -- hyper-util is the UDS transport, not a TLS client), .well-known/openid-configuration discovery, a JWKS cache with kid-miss refresh, a Validation config decision (iss/aud/leeway -- hire-grpc/src/service.rs is the local precedent and now sets leeway explicitly), and the verifying constructor itself, which claim.rs says must live beside the JWKS cache and nowhere else.

STILL OPEN AND ARGUABLY BIGGER THAN THIS BEAD: Evidence::binds_to returns true unconditionally for IdpVerified. A cached token carries a nonce from somebody else's login flow, not this request's challenge, so any token on disk converts to a claim until it expires. Decide that when writing the constructor.

ALSO: a cached token is a bearer artifact. A verified signature proves the issuer issued it, not that whoever holds it is the subject. hire reads it from the user's own cache while running as that user, which is the basis on which it reads their keyring -- stated rather than assumed."}
